title: Opslet: templated runbook primitives and safe admin utilities for automated handovers
creator: Asha Raman
description: Create 'opslet', a lightweight runtime and library that converts canonical runbook steps into idempotent, observable task primitives that can be executed by the support automation orchestrator and surfaced in the admin console. Goal: reduce manual incident handoffs, provide safe guardrails for operator actions, and make playbooks replayable and auditable. The scope focuses on core step primitives (checks, mutate, approval-gates, rollout controls), an opslet CLI for local testing, and a web preview integration in Redwood Console. This ticket covers design and implementation of primitives, audit+RBAC hooks, retries/backoff behavior, and integration points (Slack, PagerDuty, console, metrics).
acceptance_criteria: A reusable opslet library exposes >=10 primitive step types with consistent input/output schemas
All primitive steps are idempotent or have explicit compensating actions documented
Runbook execution records are emitted to audit-log topic with request_id, actor, start/end, and step-level results
Console shows a read-only replay of a runbook execution and a 'dry-run' preview mode
CLI can run a runbook in dry-run and live-run modes with --confirm flag and outputs structured JSON
RBAC checks intercept any step that performs data mutation; if the caller lacks permission, the step must fail with a clear remediation path
E2E integration test covers a sample 5-step incident play with Slack approvals and verifies metrics emitted
implementation_notes: We will implement opslet as a small Go library (to reuse existing runtime dependencies) with protobuf schemas for step payloads. The library provides an executor that can run locally or inside the support orchestrator. Steps register handlers; handlers return a standardized StepResult. To ensure safety we add a 'two-phase commit' pattern for mutating steps: plan -> approve -> apply. The console integration will fetch execution traces and render per-step artifacts. We will add feature flags to gate live-run capability per-team (console + CLI).
design_decisions: Language: Go chosen to align with current orchestration components and reduce runtime surface
Idempotency: all 'mutate' primitives require either a reversible operation or a compensating action documented in metadata
Approval model: support Slack-based ephemeral approvals and console modal approvals; both generate signed approval tokens stored in audit logs
Telemetry: emit per-step timing and error tags to the ops-metrics namespace; correlate with request_id and customer_id when present
Security: mutate paths require RBAC check; sensitive parameters are redacted in UI and audit logs and stored encrypted via KMS
testing_plan: Unit tests for each primitive handler; integration tests that spin up the orchestrator test harness and a mock Slack/PagerDuty adapter. Add chaos test that kills executor mid-run to verify compensating actions. Add a compliance smoke test that asserts no secrets are emitted in logs. E2E will be gated in CI under a 'opslet-e2e' job. Test coordinates with staging cluster and a reserved 'ops-integration' workspace.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout by team: start with SRE and Support (alpha), move to Platform (beta) and then org-wide. Steps: (1) internal alpha for SRE with CLI; (2) console preview enabled for selected workspaces; (3) enable live-run for SRE with 24/7 oncall monitoring; (4) expand to Support and collect feedback; (5) org-wide toggle. Each stage has a rollback path: disable feature flag + mark running executions as read-only. Monitor errors, step failures, and audit-volume.
risks: Accidental destructive actions if RBAC checks are incomplete
Audit log volume increase leading to higher storage costs
Operator confusion over dry-run vs live-run semantics
Integration surface area (Slack, PagerDuty, Console) increasing blast radius
